prompt:
Create the first 80-100 second silent 3D-only mathematical discovery film for the user's Math-To-Manim reverse reasoning tree, featuring ONE host: TOI-4342 / TIC 354944123. Title: "The third rhythm". The original question is how the eumemic/exoplanets repository infers a third transiting planet candidate, including orbital and spatial relationships and discovery details. Inspect local sources/ files, which are immutable snapshots of https://github.com/eumemic/exoplanets commit ec8311b19a61092ad5eae3d34e947b14485d363e read 2026-10-12. Independent primary sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2301.01370v1 (Tey et al 2023) and https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22115 (ESPRESSO 2026).
Apply actual reverse prerequisite design: root "A third planet?" decomposes in a spatial constellation into "Repeated dimming", "Orbit + sightline", "Rule out impostors"; leaves "Light + blocked area", "Period + phase", "Projection + inclination". Brief and mathematics should reason backward to known ground; teach forward light -> geometry -> orbital periods -> repeated signal -> masking -> evidence -> candidate status. All teaching objects occupy one ThreeDScene world. Fixed readable captions/formulas can be supporting labels, but NO full-screen 2D charts, flat slides, dashboard panels or unrelated topic switches. Prefer mesh sphere surfaces, orbit rings, observer line of sight, transparent directional belt/sphere, and 3D evidence points; camera moves demonstrate real depth. Surface topology: orbit path is S^1 and spherical stellar surface is S^2; explain visually only if earned, no decorative torus or spacetime gravity well. Never imply topology verifies the candidate.
Confirmed b/c: periods 5.5382498 d and 10.688716 d, original radii 2.266 and 2.415 Rearth (Tey 2023), host Mstar ~0.63 Msun, Rstar ~0.60 Rsun, temperature ~3900 K, distance 61.54 pc. Compute circular semimajor axes from Kepler a/AU=(Mstar/Msun*(P/365.25)^2)^(1/3), clearly label these model-derived approximate distances. Candidate period median 18.9082044035 d; Rp 2.207 (+0.112,-0.108) Rearth, k=Rp/Rstar=0.0337894, b=0.746895, fitted T14=2.45559 h, depth_ppm=1141.7238 from transit_fit.json. An area-based 1142 ppm illustration uses k^2 approximation for uniform disk; not a raw measured time-series. Candidate orbit should be dashed and marked "candidate", no official d designation; avoid naming the separate 47.5-d RV candidate as this signal. Omit the 47.5d orbit unless needed to explain the distinction.
Keep orbital radius ratios and angular period ratios correct, with orbital phases, eccentricities and coplanarity explicitly illustrative. Display sizes exaggerated for overview, then accurately scale a transit closeup to Rp/Rstar. Camera moves around a star reveal occultation is observer-dependent: a physical planet doesn't disappear when it crosses the back of the star and a projected circle is not an ellipse in space. If demonstrating transit directions use a sphere belt whose half angle asin((Rstar+Rp)/a) narrows for larger a; label widened schematic belt. No invented orbital normal measurements.
Discovery: known b/c transit windows are MASKED before searching residual samples; repeated candidate recovered independently by TOI-host search. Evidence in 8 sectors [13,27,66,67,93,101,102,103], old SNR=11.3393, new SNR=7.39005; do not equate sectors with transits (LEO N_transit=9). Can show sector depths with errors as 3D rods using vetting.json but avoid overcrowding. Neighbor source file nearest capable listed contaminator at 38.248 arcsec; README says none within 30 arcsec bright enough to mimic. Centroid offsets in S66 7.1, S67 15.5, S93 9.5 arcsec do not prove full localization. Gaia-constrained TRICERATOPS FPP_mean=0.1113498 over ten runs from triceratops_gaia.json, NFPP_max=1.1854e-5; use this updated value, not stale README 0.14. Finish clearly "A candidate. Confirmation still needed." FPP 0.111 exceeds statistical validation threshold 0.015; model-dependent probability, not detection confidence. Explain followup by ground photometry/high-resolution imaging/RVs, without invented confirmation.
At most one main formula and two caption lines. Use stable reusable meshes/curves (not rebuilding Surface every frame), readable typography, smooth camera motion and holds. Render quality medium 1280x720 30fps. Use actual installed Manim with modest surface complexity so local Cairo render is practical. Author specialist and evidence auditor are gpt-6-astra through official SDK with Codex login. Jev advisory only, no Jev-triggered retries. Retain failed attempts and actual evidence.
